title: Asymptotic midpoint renormability versus AUC
exact_target: Must every infinite-dimensional real Banach space that admits an asymptotically midpoint uniformly convex norm also admit an equivalent asymptotically uniformly convex norm? Positivity of the midpoint modulus is in the finite-codimensional averaged two-sided convention; AUC uses the corresponding one-sided convention.

\section*{Asymptotic midpoint renormability versus AUC}

\subsection{OpenAI's claim}
OpenAI presents the following claims relevant to this question, with manuscript numbers following paper order in Sources. In manuscript 1 (family 331; 2026-09-27), the asserted result is that a separable reflexive tree-norm space is asymptotically midpoint uniformly convex with modulus at least $\sqrt{1+t^2/12}-1$ but has no AUC renorming, and depth-$k$ diamonds incur distortion at least $\sqrt{1+k/12}$; In manuscript 2 (family 331; 2026-09-27), the asserted result is that a real measure-precompact Daugavet subspace of $L^1$ has exact averaged midpoint modulus $\max\{t/2,t-1\}$ and one-sided modulus $\max\{0,t-2\}$, and no equivalent AUC norm; In manuscript 3 (family 331; 2026-09-27), the asserted result is that path products of independent exponential or Gaussian-square variables span real $L^1$ spaces with positive midpoint moduli but no AUC renorming; In manuscript 4 (family 331; 2026-09-27), the asserted result is that four bounded-tree-potential norms have averaged midpoint lower bound $\sqrt{1+t^2/4}-1$ for $0<t<1$ but no AUC renorming, with the stated reflexive Hilbert-sum variants; In manuscript 5 (family 331; 2026-09-27), the asserted result is that recursive two-field tree norms have cubic or sixth-power midpoint bounds, including reflexive examples with no AUC equivalent norm; In manuscript 6 (family 331; 2026-09-27), the asserted result is that segment-forest duals and the infinite-height coordinate predual have small symmetric-lens tails and midpoint convexity, despite failing every AUC renorming, with reflexivity for the stated finite-height forest dual.

\subsection{Mathematical statement of the claimed result}
\paragraph{Manuscript 1.}
Let $\mathcal F=\coprod_{h\ge1}\{h\}\times\mathbb N^{\le h}$ be a forest of countably branching finite-height trees. Complete finitely supported real functions under
\[
 \rho(u)=\sup_{S_1,\ldots,S_m}\Bigl(\sum_{i=1}^m(\sum_{v\in S_i}u(v))^2\Bigr)^{1/2},
\]
where the supremum ranges over finite families of pairwise disjoint ancestral segments, and call the completion $J$. The claim states that $X=J^*$ is separable, infinite dimensional and reflexive, admits no equivalent asymptotically uniformly convex norm, and its dual norm satisfies
\[
 \widehat\delta_X(t)\ge\sqrt{1+t^2/12}-1\quad(t>0).
\]
Here $\widehat\delta_X(t)=\inf_{\|x\|=1}\sup_F\inf_{y\in F,\|y\|=1}((\|x+ty\|+\|x-ty\|)/2-1)$, with $F$ closed and finite-codimensional. Every embedding of the $k$th countably branching diamond graph, with shortest-path metric, has distortion at least $\sqrt{1+k/12}$ for every $k\ge0$.

\paragraph{Manuscript 2.}
Take a probability space $(\Omega,\mathbb P)$ and a real closed subspace $E\subseteq L^1(\Omega,\mathbb P)$ with infinite dimension. Require total boundedness of its unit ball for the topology of convergence in measure. For the restricted $L^1$ norm also require the Daugavet equation $\|I+T\|=1+\|T\|$ for every rank-one operator $T$. For $\|x\|=1$ define
\[
 H_E(x,t)=\sup_F\inf_{y\in F,\|y\|=1}((\|x+ty\|+\|x-ty\|)/2-1),
 \quad D_E(x,t)=\sup_F\inf_{y\in F,\|y\|=1}(\|x+ty\|-1),
\]
with $F$ closed finite-codimensional. The claimed exact identities are
\[
 H_E(x,t)=\max\{t/2,t-1\},\qquad D_E(x,t)=\max\{0,t-2\}\quad(t>0).
\]
These also give the infima over unit $x$, namely the averaged midpoint and AUC moduli. Such spaces are asserted to exist by the stated Kadets--Werner construction and admit no equivalent AUC norm.

\paragraph{Manuscript 3.}
On the tree $\mathbb N^{<\omega}$ take independent copies $W_v$ of a positive nonconstant real variable with $\mathbb EW=1$, $\mathbb EW^2<\infty$. Put $P_{\varnothing}=1$, $P_v=P_{v^-}W_v$ and $X_W=\overline{\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{P_v\}}^{L^1}$. Every such space is claimed infinite dimensional and to admit no equivalent AUC norm. With inherited norm, let $\widehat\delta$ use the averaged signed norms, infimum over unit centers, supremum over closed finite-codimensional $F$ and infimum over $y\in F$ of norm at least one. For exponential $W$ and $W=G^2$, $G$ standard normal, define $c(K)=\mathbb E(|G|-2K)_+/16$. The claimed positive estimates are
\[
 \widehat\delta_{X_{\rm exp}}(t)\ge(7t/30)c(10/t),\quad
 \widehat\delta_{X_{\rm sq}}(t)\ge\Pr(|G|\ge4\sqrt2(2+\sqrt2)/t)/8,
 \quad\widehat\delta_{X_{\rm sq}}(t)\ge\Pr(|G|\ge8\sqrt6/t)/4
\]
for every $t>0$.

\paragraph{Manuscript 4.}
Let $T=\mathbb N^{<\omega}$, root $o$, and $P_f(s)=\sum_{u\in I,\ u\preceq s}f_u$. Four symmetric test sets all require $|P_f(s)|\le1$. The root-free sibling set uses $I=T\setminus\{o\}$ and $\sum_{u\in\operatorname{ch}(r)}f_u^2\le1$; the root-inclusive sibling set uses $I=T$ with that same constraint. The antichain set uses finitely supported $f$ on $T$ and $\sum_{u\in A}f_u^2\le1$ for every finite antichain. The global set uses $f\in\ell_2(T)$ with $\sum_Tf_u^2\le1$. Complete finite vectors in $\|x\|_K=\sup_{f\in K}\sum_s f_sx_s$ to obtain $X_K$. Each is claimed separable infinite dimensional, has no equivalent AUC norm, and has averaged midpoint modulus
\[
 \widehat\delta_{X_K}(t)\ge\sqrt{1+t^2/4}-1\quad(0<t<1).
\]
For the segment construction, use disjoint component trees $\mathcal T_n=\mathbb N^{\le n}$, $n\ge1$. On nonnegative arrays recursively define
\[
 q_t(m)=m_t+(\sum_{u\in\operatorname{ch}(t)}q_u(m)^2)^{1/2},\qquad M_n(m)=q_{\varnothing}(m).
\]
A segment array $(a_{tv})_{t\preceq v}$ has start masses $m_t(a)=\sum_{v\succeq t}|a_{tv}|$ and output $(Pa)_s=\sum_{t\preceq s}\sum_{v\succeq s}a_{tv}$. Set
\[
 \|x\|_{S,n}=\inf_{Pa=x}M_n(m(a)),\qquad
 X_S=\left(\bigoplus_{n\ge1}(\ell_2(\mathcal T_n),\|\cdot\|_{S,n})\right)_{\ell_2}.
\]
The claimed complete component norms satisfy $\|x\|_2/(n+1)\le\|x\|_{S,n}\le\sqrt{n+1}\|x\|_2$, and supply a reflexive $X_S$ with contractive finite ancestral coordinate projections, unit coordinate and root-to-node path vectors, and weakly null sibling sequences; its maximum midpoint modulus satisfies
\[
 \delta^{\max}_{X_S}(t)\ge\sqrt{1+t^2/64}-1\quad(t>0).
\]
Both midpoint moduli take the infimum over unit centers, supremum over closed finite-codimensional subspaces and infimum over their large directions; the first uses the average of the two signed norms, the second their maximum.

\paragraph{Manuscript 5.}
For finitely supported real vectors on a rooted countably branching tree, compute upward from zero fields below the support:
\[
 A_s=(\sum_{c\in\operatorname{ch}(s)}P_c^2)^{1/2},\quad
 B_s=(\sum_{c\in\operatorname{ch}(s)}Q_c^2)^{1/2},\quad
 P_s=\max\{A_s,v_s+B_s\},\quad Q_s=\max\{B_s,-v_s+A_s\}.
\]
On $\mathbb N^{<\omega}$ let $N_{\Sigma}=P_o+Q_o$. Join disjoint trees $\mathbb N^{\le n}$, $n\ge1$, under a new root $\rho$; with $v_{\rho}=0$ let $N_0=P_{\rho}=Q_{\rho}$, and with that coordinate free let $N_J=P_{\rho}+Q_{\rho}$. Complete to $X_{\Sigma},X_0,X_J$. All are claimed Banach spaces with no equivalent AUC norm, and $X_0,X_J$ are reflexive. The averaged midpoint estimates are
\[
 \widehat\delta_{N_{\Sigma}}(t),\widehat\delta_{N_J}(t)\ge t^3/128\quad(0<t<1).
\]
If $H$ is finite ancestral, $x$ supported in $H$, and $0\ne z$ vanishes on $H$, the further estimate is
\[
 \frac{N_0(x+z)+N_0(x-z)}2\ge N_0(x)+\frac{N_0(z)^3}{8(2N_0(x)+N_0(z))^2}.
\]
Coordinate restrictions to finite ancestral sets are contractive, their kernels finite-codimensional, and finite-support vectors dense there.

\paragraph{Manuscript 6.}
Complete finitely supported real arrays on the forest $\coprod_{h\ge1}\mathbb N^{\le h}$ in the norm $\rho(a)=\sup(\sum_j|\sum_{v\in S_j}a_v|^2)^{1/2}$ over finite disjoint ancestral segments, and set $X=J^*$. Define the same segment completion $J_{\infty}$ on $\mathbb N^{<\omega}$ and let $B_{\infty}$ be the closed span of coordinate evaluations in $J_{\infty}^*$. For either $Y=X$ or $B_{\infty}$, finite ancestral $H$, $P_H$ coordinate restriction, $Q_H=I-P_H$, $x=P_Hx$ and $\|x\pm y\|\le R$, the asserted lens estimate is
\[
 \|Q_Hy\|\le2\sqrt{R^2-\|x\|^2}.
\]
Its averaged midpoint consequence is $\widehat\delta_Y(t)\ge(\sqrt{1+t^2/4}-1)/2$ for every $t>0$. The finite-height dual is claimed separable reflexive, with dense coordinate span and contractive ancestral projections. For any unbounded sequence of finite component heights and equivalent norm $N$ satisfying $a\|x\|\le N(x)\le b\|x\|$, it claims
\[
 \overline\delta_N(a/b)=\overline\delta_N(a/(2b))=0,
\]
so there is no equivalent AUC norm. Here the one-sided modulus is $\inf_{N(x)=1}\sup_F\inf_{y\in F,N(y)=1}(N(x+ty)-1)$.

\subsection{Outline of the argument}
For manuscript 1 (family 331; 2026-09-27), paired segment tests bound approximate midpoint tails in the coordinate completion. Fresh layers along a branching diamond accumulate an energy loss at each level, while uniformly bounded branches persist under equivalent norms and obstruct one-sided asymptotic convexity. For manuscript 2 (family 331; 2026-09-27), a quantitative finite-dimensional enlargement constructs the required subspace. Compact clipping leaves a fixed mass outside each head, while almost diametral weak-neighborhood points give matching upper tests; the same directions exclude one-sided convexification under every renorming.

For manuscript 3 (family 331; 2026-09-27), fresh multipliers are conditioned along finite tree heads. Gaussian scale-mixture identities or scalar square estimates force uniform excess for every coefficient list, giving midpoint growth, whereas bounded positive-mean paths obstruct every one-sided renorming. For manuscript 4 (family 331; 2026-09-27), two inward tests split the tail of an arbitrary dual potential relative to a head norming functional. Clipping and subtree quotas bound path coefficients, while newly exposed coordinate energy gives midpoint growth; bounded branches survive all equivalent norms.

For manuscript 5 (family 331; 2026-09-27), least positive fields represent the vector through their difference. Root defects propagate until a stopping boundary, where accumulated Euclidean energy yields the midpoint estimate; finite-height Hilbert equivalence proves reflexivity, while bounded paths prevent AUC renorming. For manuscript 6 (family 331; 2026-09-27), finite convex laws are recovered by clipping cumulative segment sums and matching opposite masses at boundary crossings. Endpoint comparisons bound the tail by the squared-radius deficit, and completed atomic laws transfer the estimate to the specified spaces.

\subsection{Scope relative to this problem}
The displayed question has a negative answer under the manuscript's stated construction. Its counterexample meets the conditions in this problem and defeats the universal assertion, so this is a full disproof claim. The supporting results are manuscript 2 (family 331; 2026-09-27), manuscript 3 (family 331; 2026-09-27), manuscript 4 (family 331; 2026-09-27), manuscript 5 (family 331; 2026-09-27), manuscript 6 (family 331; 2026-09-27). Other linked papers contribute only their stated special cases; those weaker results alone would not resolve the complete question.

\subsection{Formal verification}
For manuscript 1 (family 331; 2026-09-27), the documented Lean scope is the specified segment-space dual, its midpoint modulus $\sqrt{1+t^2/12}-1$, and its separability, reflexivity, renorming obstruction, and diamond-distortion estimate; extensions to general forests concern a closed coordinate span and do not assert these conclusions for every full forest dual.

The central assertion is within the documented formal scope; the additional applications retain their own scope limits.

For manuscript 2 (family 331; 2026-09-27), OpenAI lists Lean statements for this assertion: a real measure-precompact Daugavet subspace of $L^1$ has exact averaged midpoint modulus $\max\{t/2,t-1\}$ and one-sided modulus $\max\{0,t-2\}$, and no equivalent AUC norm.

This coverage does not establish a formal proof of the complete problem as stated here.

For manuscript 3 (family 331; 2026-09-27), OpenAI lists Lean statements for this assertion: path products of independent exponential or Gaussian-square variables span real $L^1$ spaces with positive midpoint moduli but no AUC renorming.

This coverage does not establish a formal proof of the complete problem as stated here.

For manuscript 4 (family 331; 2026-09-27), the documented Lean scope is the stated tree-potential completions and their midpoint modulus, completeness, separability, and obstruction to asymptotic uniform convexity; the selected path-cost and comparison statements retain their support and head-tail hypotheses, and the remaining auxiliary assertions are outside this scope.

This coverage does not establish a formal proof of the complete problem as stated here.

For manuscript 5 (family 331; 2026-09-27), the documented Lean scope is the root-sum and joined-space midpoint bound $t^3/128$ for $0<t<1$, the stated zero-root tail estimates with finite-ancestor support, and the selected reflexivity conclusions for the joined and zero-root spaces; variable-exponent comparisons retain their sequence and head conditions.

This coverage does not establish a formal proof of the complete problem as stated here.

For manuscript 6 (family 331; 2026-09-27), the documented Lean scope is the tail estimate $2\sqrt{R^2-\lVert x\rVert^2}$ for centers supported on a finite ancestral head, under the two radius inequalities, in the specified finite-height dual and infinite-tree coordinate settings; the selected duality and renorming conclusions retain those forest assumptions.

This coverage does not establish a formal proof of the complete problem as stated here.

\subsection{Status caveat}
The manuscripts were produced by an internal OpenAI model. OpenAI cautions that results without formalization can contain mistakes. This site has not independently checked the proofs; the label records the scope of OpenAI's claim.

\section*{Asymptotic midpoint renormability versus AUC}

\subsection{OpenAI's claim}
OpenAI presents the following claims relevant to this question, with manuscript numbers following paper order in Sources. In manuscript 1 (family 331; 2026-09-27), the asserted result is that a separable reflexive tree-norm space is asymptotically midpoint uniformly convex with modulus at least $\sqrt{1+t^2/12}-1$ but has no AUC renorming, and depth-$k$ diamonds incur distortion at least $\sqrt{1+k/12}$; In manuscript 2 (family 331; 2026-09-27), the asserted result is that a real measure-precompact Daugavet subspace of $L^1$ has exact averaged midpoint modulus $\max\{t/2,t-1\}$ and one-sided modulus $\max\{0,t-2\}$, and no equivalent AUC norm; In manuscript 3 (family 331; 2026-09-27), the asserted result is that path products of independent exponential or Gaussian-square variables span real $L^1$ spaces with positive midpoint moduli but no AUC renorming; In manuscript 4 (family 331; 2026-09-27), the asserted result is that four bounded-tree-potential norms have averaged midpoint lower bound $\sqrt{1+t^2/4}-1$ for $0<t<1$ but no AUC renorming, with the stated reflexive Hilbert-sum variants; In manuscript 5 (family 331; 2026-09-27), the asserted result is that recursive two-field tree norms have cubic or sixth-power midpoint bounds, including reflexive examples with no AUC equivalent norm; In manuscript 6 (family 331; 2026-09-27), the asserted result is that segment-forest duals and the infinite-height coordinate predual have small symmetric-lens tails and midpoint convexity, despite failing every AUC renorming, with reflexivity for the stated finite-height forest dual.

\subsection{Mathematical statement of the claimed result}
\paragraph{Manuscript 1.}
Let $\mathcal F=\coprod_{h\ge1}\{h\}\times\mathbb N^{\le h}$ be a forest of countably branching finite-height trees. Complete finitely supported real functions under
\[
 \rho(u)=\sup_{S_1,\ldots,S_m}\Bigl(\sum_{i=1}^m(\sum_{v\in S_i}u(v))^2\Bigr)^{1/2},
\]
where the supremum ranges over finite families of pairwise disjoint ancestral segments, and call the completion $J$. The claim states that $X=J^*$ is separable, infinite dimensional and reflexive, admits no equivalent asymptotically uniformly convex norm, and its dual norm satisfies
\[
 \widehat\delta_X(t)\ge\sqrt{1+t^2/12}-1\quad(t>0).
\]
Here $\widehat\delta_X(t)=\inf_{\|x\|=1}\sup_F\inf_{y\in F,\|y\|=1}((\|x+ty\|+\|x-ty\|)/2-1)$, with $F$ closed and finite-codimensional. Every embedding of the $k$th countably branching diamond graph, with shortest-path metric, has distortion at least $\sqrt{1+k/12}$ for every $k\ge0$.

\paragraph{Manuscript 2.}
Take a probability space $(\Omega,\mathbb P)$ and a real closed subspace $E\subseteq L^1(\Omega,\mathbb P)$ with infinite dimension. Require total boundedness of its unit ball for the topology of convergence in measure. For the restricted $L^1$ norm also require the Daugavet equation $\|I+T\|=1+\|T\|$ for every rank-one operator $T$. For $\|x\|=1$ define
\[
 H_E(x,t)=\sup_F\inf_{y\in F,\|y\|=1}((\|x+ty\|+\|x-ty\|)/2-1),
 \quad D_E(x,t)=\sup_F\inf_{y\in F,\|y\|=1}(\|x+ty\|-1),
\]
with $F$ closed finite-codimensional. The claimed exact identities are
\[
 H_E(x,t)=\max\{t/2,t-1\},\qquad D_E(x,t)=\max\{0,t-2\}\quad(t>0).
\]
These also give the infima over unit $x$, namely the averaged midpoint and AUC moduli. Such spaces are asserted to exist by the stated Kadets--Werner construction and admit no equivalent AUC norm.

\paragraph{Manuscript 3.}
On the tree $\mathbb N^{<\omega}$ take independent copies $W_v$ of a positive nonconstant real variable with $\mathbb EW=1$, $\mathbb EW^2<\infty$. Put $P_{\varnothing}=1$, $P_v=P_{v^-}W_v$ and $X_W=\overline{\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{P_v\}}^{L^1}$. Every such space is claimed infinite dimensional and to admit no equivalent AUC norm. With inherited norm, let $\widehat\delta$ use the averaged signed norms, infimum over unit centers, supremum over closed finite-codimensional $F$ and infimum over $y\in F$ of norm at least one. For exponential $W$ and $W=G^2$, $G$ standard normal, define $c(K)=\mathbb E(|G|-2K)_+/16$. The claimed positive estimates are
\[
 \widehat\delta_{X_{\rm exp}}(t)\ge(7t/30)c(10/t),\quad
 \widehat\delta_{X_{\rm sq}}(t)\ge\Pr(|G|\ge4\sqrt2(2+\sqrt2)/t)/8,
 \quad\widehat\delta_{X_{\rm sq}}(t)\ge\Pr(|G|\ge8\sqrt6/t)/4
\]
for every $t>0$.

\paragraph{Manuscript 4.}
Let $T=\mathbb N^{<\omega}$, root $o$, and $P_f(s)=\sum_{u\in I,\ u\preceq s}f_u$. Four symmetric test sets all require $|P_f(s)|\le1$. The root-free sibling set uses $I=T\setminus\{o\}$ and $\sum_{u\in\operatorname{ch}(r)}f_u^2\le1$; the root-inclusive sibling set uses $I=T$ with that same constraint. The antichain set uses finitely supported $f$ on $T$ and $\sum_{u\in A}f_u^2\le1$ for every finite antichain. The global set uses $f\in\ell_2(T)$ with $\sum_Tf_u^2\le1$. Complete finite vectors in $\|x\|_K=\sup_{f\in K}\sum_s f_sx_s$ to obtain $X_K$. Each is claimed separable infinite dimensional, has no equivalent AUC norm, and has averaged midpoint modulus
\[
 \widehat\delta_{X_K}(t)\ge\sqrt{1+t^2/4}-1\quad(0<t<1).
\]
For the segment construction, use disjoint component trees $\mathcal T_n=\mathbb N^{\le n}$, $n\ge1$. On nonnegative arrays recursively define
\[
 q_t(m)=m_t+(\sum_{u\in\operatorname{ch}(t)}q_u(m)^2)^{1/2},\qquad M_n(m)=q_{\varnothing}(m).
\]
A segment array $(a_{tv})_{t\preceq v}$ has start masses $m_t(a)=\sum_{v\succeq t}|a_{tv}|$ and output $(Pa)_s=\sum_{t\preceq s}\sum_{v\succeq s}a_{tv}$. Set
\[
 \|x\|_{S,n}=\inf_{Pa=x}M_n(m(a)),\qquad
 X_S=\left(\bigoplus_{n\ge1}(\ell_2(\mathcal T_n),\|\cdot\|_{S,n})\right)_{\ell_2}.
\]
The claimed complete component norms satisfy $\|x\|_2/(n+1)\le\|x\|_{S,n}\le\sqrt{n+1}\|x\|_2$, and supply a reflexive $X_S$ with contractive finite ancestral coordinate projections, unit coordinate and root-to-node path vectors, and weakly null sibling sequences; its maximum midpoint modulus satisfies
\[
 \delta^{\max}_{X_S}(t)\ge\sqrt{1+t^2/64}-1\quad(t>0).
\]
Both midpoint moduli take the infimum over unit centers, supremum over closed finite-codimensional subspaces and infimum over their large directions; the first uses the average of the two signed norms, the second their maximum.

\paragraph{Manuscript 5.}
For finitely supported real vectors on a rooted countably branching tree, compute upward from zero fields below the support:
\[
 A_s=(\sum_{c\in\operatorname{ch}(s)}P_c^2)^{1/2},\quad
 B_s=(\sum_{c\in\operatorname{ch}(s)}Q_c^2)^{1/2},\quad

\]
On $\mathbb N^{<\omega}$ let $N_{\Sigma}=P_o+Q_o$. Join disjoint trees $\mathbb N^{\le n}$, $n\ge1$, under a new root $\rho$; with $v_{\rho}=0$ let $N_0=P_{\rho}=Q_{\rho}$, and with that coordinate free let $N_J=P_{\rho}+Q_{\rho}$. \[
 \widehat\delta_{N_{\Sigma}}(t),\widehat\delta_{N_J}(t)\ge t^3/128\quad(0<t<1).
\]
If $H$ is finite ancestral, $x$ supported in $H$, and $0\ne z$ vanishes on $H$, the further estimate is
\[
 \frac{N_0(x+z)+N_0(x-z)}2\ge N_0(x)+\frac{N_0(z)^3}{8(2N_0(x)+N_0(z))^2}.
\]
Coordinate restrictions to finite ancestral sets are contractive, their kernels finite-codimensional, and finite-support vectors dense there.

\paragraph{Manuscript 6.}
Complete finitely supported real arrays on the forest $\coprod_{h\ge1}\mathbb N^{\le h}$ in the norm $\rho(a)=\sup(\sum_j|\sum_{v\in S_j}a_v|^2)^{1/2}$ over finite disjoint ancestral segments, and set $X=J^*$. \]

\subsection{Outline of the argument}
For manuscript 1 (family 331; 2026-09-27), paired segment tests bound approximate midpoint tails in the coordinate completion. Fresh layers along a branching diamond accumulate an energy loss at each level, while uniformly bounded branches persist under equivalent norms and obstruct one-sided asymptotic convexity. For manuscript 2 (family 331; 2026-09-27), a quantitative finite-dimensional enlargement constructs the required subspace. Compact clipping leaves a fixed mass outside each head, while almost diametral weak-neighborhood points give matching upper tests; the same directions exclude one-sided convexification under every renorming.

For manuscript 3 (family 331; 2026-09-27), fresh multipliers are conditioned along finite tree heads. Gaussian scale-mixture identities or scalar square estimates force uniform excess for every coefficient list, giving midpoint growth, whereas bounded positive-mean paths obstruct every one-sided renorming. For manuscript 4 (family 331; 2026-09-27), two inward tests split the tail of an arbitrary dual potential relative to a head norming functional. Clipping and subtree quotas bound path coefficients, while newly exposed coordinate energy gives midpoint growth; bounded branches survive all equivalent norms.

For manuscript 5 (family 331; 2026-09-27), least positive fields represent the vector through their difference. Root defects propagate until a stopping boundary, where accumulated Euclidean energy yields the midpoint estimate; finite-height Hilbert equivalence proves reflexivity, while bounded paths prevent AUC renorming. For manuscript 6 (family 331; 2026-09-27), finite convex laws are recovered by clipping cumulative segment sums and matching opposite masses at boundary crossings. Endpoint comparisons bound the tail by the squared-radius deficit, and completed atomic laws transfer the estimate to the specified spaces.
